messages:
hao: heads up — we've got a spike in exported spans from the text-infer workers. looks like per-token spans (kv-cache/token) are blowing up retention. any recommended SDK patterns for python/go/rust here? @maria @nate :thinking:

maria: don't create a span per token. two patterns we've used: 1) aggregate tokens into a single span with events (add_event) for tokens, or 2) emit metrics (counters/histograms) for token counts and latencies and keep traces sparse. both reduce span cardinality.

nate: +1 to aggregate. also use BatchSpanProcessor and configure max_queue_size + schedule_delay to avoid tiny exports. for python: use OTLPSpanExporter -> BatchSpanProcessor(resource=Resource({"service.name": "text-infer", "model.name": os.getenv('MODEL_NAME', 'unknown')})) and for rust/go similar processors exist.

jess: note: events still show up in tracing UI and can be heavy depending on backend. if you need per-token observability for debugging, add a toggle via env var or route-level flag, default off.

sam: consider exporter multiplexing: traces sampled 1-5% -> tracing backend, metrics/aggregates always -> metrics backend. we can also route high-cardinality route spans to a special low-retention bucket.

hao: what about agent vs direct OTLP? we currently have two patterns across services which is messy for ops.

maria: prefer agent for network control + batching at host level, but agent needs config to avoid additional fanout. direct OTLP is fine if we set batching well. whichever we pick, make sure language sdk init is consistent so we don't get mixed headers.

nate: another gotcha: sampling at SDK level will drop spans before exporters see them which also affects events/attributes metrics that we might rely on. if we want metrics to be independent, emit metrics via the metrics API instead of relying on spans.

jess: sample code for lightweight python init (quick):
```python
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.sdk.resources import Resource
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor, OTLPSpanExporter

resource = Resource.create({"service.name": "text-infer", "model.name": os.getenv('MODEL_NAME', 'unknown')})
provider = TracerProvider(resource=resource)
exporter = OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint=os.getenv('OTEL_ENDPOINT'))
provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(exporter, max_queue_size=2048, schedule_delay_millis=200))
trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)
```

sam: for go/rust we should add a shared helper that sets Resource attrs (model.name, route, deployment_id) and env toggles: OTEL_TOKEN_FANOUT=off, OTEL_FANOUT_SAMPLE=0.01. keep defaults conservative.

hao: how do we surface this in the console? dashboards need to reflect sampling and retention so SREs don't get surprised by missing traces.

maria: console needs two things: 1) route-level telemetry panel showing tokens-per-request histogram and export rate, 2) visible sampling and exporter config for each deployment. make sampling a first-class toggle in rollout UX.

nate: ops action: add telemetry-lint check in CI that warns if service registers per-token spans or sets extremely low BatchSpanProcessor queue sizes.

dev-bot: deploy canary: telemetry-helpers v0.4 -> staging (sha: d4c3b2) :rocket:

hao: decision / next steps: 1) implement language helper libs (py/go/rust) that do: aggregate token events into span events by default, export metrics for token counts, standard resource attrs, BatchSpanProcessor defaults. 2) docs + console visibility for sampling & exporter. 3) ops: prefer agent but ensure agent-level dedup/aggregation. i'll open RFC/PRs for each language. tagging owners: @maria (py), @nate (go), @jess (rust).

jess: ack, will draft rust helper and add tests for graceful shutdown flush (sdk shutdown must call flush in our runtime).

sam: i'll sketch console toggles this afternoon and link to the RFC. :thumbsup:

hao: thanks all — lets keep per-token observability gated and default to aggregate/metrics.
